english.title: Use a motor vehicle on a road / public place without third party insurance
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) used a motor vehicle, namely **(..SPECIFY VEHICLE MAKE AND INDEX NUMBER..), on a road, or other public place, namely **(..SPECIFY THE ROAD OR PUBLIC PLACE AND LOCATION..), when there was not in force in relation to that use such a policy of insurance or such a security in respect of third party risks as complied with the requirements of Part VI of the Road Traffic Act 1988
english.legislation: Contrary to section 143 of the Road Traffic Act1988 and Schedule 2 to the Road Traffic Offenders Act 1988.

english.notes:
(i) Statement of Facts procedure applies - see end of document for wording.
(ii) See also offence wordings: H47 and H48.
(iii) This offence was extended to include 'other public place' by the The Motor Vehicles (Compulsory Insurance) Regulations 2000 - S.I. 726/2000 refers.
(iv) Fixed penalty procedure may be applied
(v) There is a common term in insurance policies which usually states something along the lines that the driver is covered if s/he holds or has held a driving licence to drive the vehicle (i.e. that class of vehicle) and is not disqualified. We are assuming everything else in the certificate is in order. If this term is in the certificate of insurance (and the driver is not disqualified by a court), s/he is covered by the insurance whether or not s/he does or does not hold a current UK/foreign/provisional licence for that class of vehicle, as long as s/he held one in the past. (Above based on Edwards v Griffiths 1953) However, the term can vary on occasions, so it is worth reading the certificate carefully.
(iv) From 1st November 2019, the Motor Vehicles (Compulsory Insurance) (Miscellaneous Amendments) Regulations 2019 (SI 2019/1047) removed the current securities regime, which was used as an alternative to conventional motor insurance. A two-year transitional period applied to existing securities and deposits; this meant that new securities could not be issued, however, it did not prevent individuals renewing current securities - as long as they were valid until 1st November 2021. From 1st November 2021 compulsory motor insurance is required. For the offence applying from the 1st November 2021, see H100080.
